title: Kojima et al. 2024 (Dataset A) — An auditory brain-computer interface based on selective attention to multiple tone streams
description: This dataset comprises 64-channel EEG recordings from 11 healthy subjects performing an auditory P300-based brain-computer interface task using selective attention to multiple tone streams. Subjects attended to one of three auditory streams of musical tones and counted target stimuli while P300 activity was recorded. Classification using Riemannian geometry achieved >80% accuracy for 5 subjects and >75% for 9 subjects, demonstrating the feasibility of multi-class auditory BCIs based on auditory stream segregation.
methods_description: EEG and EOG signals were recorded at 1000 Hz from 11 subjects using 64 EEG channels and 2 EOG channels (Brain Amp DC and MR plus amplifiers, EASYCAP electrodes, right earlobe reference). Musical tones (150 ms duration, 180 ms stimulus onset asynchrony) were presented to the right ear via headphones. Each experiment consisted of two task blocks with three 5-minute runs. Subjects counted target stimuli (10% probability) in attended streams while ignoring non-target stimuli (90% probability). Data were bandpass filtered (0.1-40 Hz for ERP, 1-40 Hz for classification), baseline corrected, artifact rejected, and classified using xDAWN spatial filtering with Riemannian geometry covariance matrices.
